key_insight: PSDesigner automates graphic design by emulating a human-like creative workflow—producing editable, layered design files from user intent through iterative ideation, composition, and refinement steps.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between generative image models and real-world design practice by translating user instructions into flexible, editable design assets and layouts that support professional, iterative workflows.
method: Human-like multi-stage pipeline: ideation (concept generation), composition (layout & asset placement), and refinement (iterative edits and finalization).
Combines text-to-image models for asset creation, a layout engine for structured, editable compositions, and an MLLM controller to parse intent and drive iterative decisions.
Outputs production-ready editable files (layered/SVG/PSD-like formats) and supports human-in-the-loop edits for fine-grained control.
impact: Enables practitioners to generate production-ready, editable designs quickly while preserving professional flexibility and interpretability, accelerating creative workflows and enabling new research on controllable generative design tools.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing ideation → composition → refinement with icons for text input, image generator, layout engine, and editable file output.
Before/after comparison: simple prompt → final editable layered design file (showing layers and selectable elements).
Interface mockup illustrating iterative human-in-the-loop edits and automated suggestions.
Bar/radar chart comparing flexibility, editability, and realism against prior end-to-end text-to-image approaches.
paper_title: PSDesigner: Automated Graphic Design with a Human-Like Creative Workflow
paper_authors: Xincheng Shuai, Song Tang, Yutong Huang, Henghui Ding, Dacheng Tao
